problems.title: Order three trigonometric values
problems.question: Order a=tan280°,b=sin18°,c=cos18° increasingly.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Tangent is negative in quadrant IV; for 0°<t<45°, sin t<cos t.
steps: a<0, while 0<b<c. Thus a<b<c.

problems.title: A minimum of a sine square
problems.question: Find the minimum of sin²(x²−πx+3).
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Sine squares are nonnegative; zero is attained if the inner expression is an integer multiple of π.
steps: The inner quadratic has range [3−π²/4,∞), which contains π. Thus some real x makes it equal π, and the sine square is zero.

problems.title: An equation ruled out by incompatible bounds
problems.question: Solve 2sin x cos x=1/x+x.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Left side=sin2x∈[−1,1]; for real nonzero x, |x+1/x|≥2.
steps: The ranges cannot overlap. x=0 is outside the equation’s domain.

problems.title: Skew-line pairs from four coplanar points and an apex
problems.question: Four points lie in a plane and a fifth P lies outside it. Lines join each pair. Count skew-line pairs.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: In general position, each line PA is skew to the three base lines joining two of the other three points.
steps: If no three base points are collinear, each of the four apex lines gives three skew pairs, totaling 12. Base-base pairs are coplanar; apex-apex pairs meet at P.
The stated text does not exclude collinearity. If all four base points are collinear, there are no skew pairs at all.
problems.note: A no-three-collinear condition is needed for a unique count. The literal data also permit configurations with fewer skew pairs.

problems.title: Sector area in radians
problems.question: A circle has radius √2 and sector angle alpha radians, alpha<π. Find the sector area.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Sector area $=R^2\alpha/2$.
steps: R²=2, so the area is alpha.

problems.title: Double-angle sine from a tangent
problems.question: tan a=5. Find sin2a.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: $\sin2a=2\tan a/(1+\tan^2a)$.
steps: The value is 10/(1+25)=5/13.

problems.title: The sign of an odd sine power
problems.question: If sin³alpha>0, which quadrants may alpha occupy?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: An odd power preserves sign.
steps: sin alpha>0, which holds in quadrants I and II. Axis angles do not satisfy strict positivity.

problems.title: Count even functions
problems.question: How many are even: sin²x,cos5x,x⁴/|x+2|,cos³x,−cos x,(tan x+sin x)²?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Check f(−x)=f(x) and symmetry of the domain.
steps: sin²x,cos5x,cos³x,−cos x are even. tan x+sin x is odd on a symmetric domain, so its square is even.
x⁴/|x+2| is not even and its exclusion x=−2 is not symmetric. Thus five qualify.

problems.title: Regular polygons obtainable as cube sections
problems.question: Which regular polygons can occur as planar cube sections?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: A plane meets at most six cube faces; opposite face planes produce parallel section sides.
steps: A corner cut x+y+z=t makes an equilateral triangle; a face-parallel cut makes a square; a central cut x+y+z=3/2 in the unit cube makes a regular hexagon.
A five-sided section must use five of six faces, including opposite pairs, so it has parallel side pairs. A regular pentagon has none, and therefore cannot occur.
problems.answer: Equilateral triangle, square and regular hexagon.

problems.title: A line parallel to a plane
problems.question: If a line is parallel to a plane, what parallel line must exist inside the plane?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: A plane contains a line through any chosen point in any direction parallel to it.
steps: The given line’s direction lies parallel to the plane. A line in that direction through a point of the plane is parallel to it.
It need not be parallel to arbitrary lines or two intersecting lines of the plane.

problems.title: Least period of a sine-square plus tangent
problems.question: Find the least positive period of sin²3x+tan3x.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: sin²t and tan t both have period π.
steps: π/3 is a period of both terms. The tangent’s pole set is spaced π/3 apart and must be preserved by a period, so no smaller positive period is possible.

problems.title: A trigonometric fraction using tangent
problems.question: Find (sin x−cos x)/(2sin x+3cos x) if tan x=3.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Divide by cos x, which is nonzero.
steps: The fraction becomes (tan x−1)/(2tan x+3)=(3−1)/(6+3)=2/9.

problems.title: Sine of a difference with acute constraints
problems.question: sin(alpha+beta)=1/3, sin alpha=1/5, and 0<alpha,beta<π/4. Find sin beta.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: $\sin\beta=\sin(\alpha+\beta)\cos\alpha-\cos(\alpha+\beta)\sin\alpha$.
steps: The restrictions make alpha+beta acute. Thus cos alpha=2√6/5 and cos(alpha+beta)=2√2/3.
Substitute to obtain (2√6−2√2)/15.

problems.title: An unrestricted displacement along intersecting planes
problems.question: Planes meet on a line b. A and B have distances 5 and 7 from b in their respective planes. How many of 10,12,14,15,16,17 can be their distance?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: For perpendicular planes, AB²=5²+7²+t², where t is the difference of coordinates along b.
steps: For every listed D≥10, choose t=√(D²−74). This is real and realizes AB=D.
Thus all six listed distances are possible; a bound of 12 would ignore displacement along b.

problems.title: Maximum intersection lines of fifteen planes
problems.question: Fifteen planes are given. What is the maximum number of their distinct intersection lines?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Each plane pair determines at most one line.
steps: There are C(15,2)=15×14/2=105 pairs. Generic planes can have no parallel pairs and no three sharing a line, attaining that count.

problems.title: A number equal to its fractional part
problems.question: Solve {x}=x, where braces denote fractional part.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: {x}=x−floor(x), so equality means floor(x)=0.
steps: This holds exactly when 0≤x<1.

problems.title: A downward quadratic cannot meet a positive horizontal line
problems.question: Count intersections of y=(sin4)x²+(sin4)x−1 and y=cos56°sin31°+sin56°sin34°.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: 4 is in radians, so sin4<0; complete x²+x=(x+1/2)²−1/4.
steps: The first function’s maximum is −1−sin4/4, which is at most −3/4 because sin4≥−1.
The second function is a positive constant, since all its displayed degree-angle sine and cosine factors are positive. Thus the graphs cannot meet.

problems.title: A radical whose domain is a discrete set
problems.question: Find the least positive period of $\sqrt{\pi-\pi/\sin^2x}$.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Domain requires sin²x>0 and 1−1/sin²x≥0.
steps: Since sin²x≤1, the condition forces sin²x=1. Thus x=π/2+kπ, and the function equals zero on this domain.
The least translation preserving this entire domain is π, so the least positive period is π.
problems.note: The function is defined only at x=π/2+kπ. Its period must preserve that domain, so being zero there does not make every positive number a period.

problems.title: Orthogonal directions versus intersecting perpendicular lines
problems.question: Line a is parallel to plane beta. How many lines in beta are perpendicular to a?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Angle between spatial lines can be defined using their direction vectors.
steps: For direction orthogonality, the plane contains a perpendicular direction to a. Every parallel translate in that direction gives another such line, so there are infinitely many.
If “perpendicular” is defined to require actual intersection, none can qualify because a has no point in beta.
problems.answer: Infinitely many under the spatial direction-angle convention.
problems.note: If perpendicular lines must intersect, the alternative answer is zero. The distinction matters here because the given line is disjoint from the plane.

problems.title: Interpolate a distance without crossing a plane
problems.question: AB does not cross a plane, with endpoint distances 10,22. K divides AK:KB=1:3. Find its distance.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Signed distance is affine; same-side distances can be averaged directly.
steps: K is one quarter of the way from A to B. Its distance is (3×10+22)/4=13.

problems.title: Reduce three large angles
problems.question: Evaluate tan199°sin720°+tan1990°cos450°+sin810°.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: sin720°=0, cos450°=0, sin810°=1; the tangents are defined.
steps: The first two terms vanish and the last is 1.

problems.title: A parameter gives a half-turn period
problems.question: For which a is π a period of f(x)=sin x/(a−cos x)?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: f(x+π)=−sin x/(a+cos x).
steps: Equating with f(x) at inputs with nonzero sine gives −(a−cos x)=a+cos x, hence a=0.
At a=0 the function is −tan x, whose domain and values repeat with π.

problems.title: A radical denominator and a sine cube
problems.question: Which listed x satisfies $\sin^3x/\sqrt{1-\sin^2x}+\sin^2x-1=0$?
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Domain |sin x|<1; set t=sin x and use positivity of the denominator.
steps: The equation is t³=(1−t²)³/². The right side is positive, so t>0. Taking cube roots gives t=√(1−t²).
Thus t=1/√2. The full solutions are π/4+2kπ and 3π/4+2kπ; among the listed inputs, only π/4 works.

problems.title: Angle between two lines in a cube
problems.question: K is midpoint of DD₁ in cube ABCDA₁B₁C₁D₁. Find the cosine between CK and A₁D.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
formulas: Use unit-cube coordinates and the absolute dot product for the smaller line angle.
steps: The absolute dot product is 1/2; length product is √(5/4)√2=√10/2. The cosine is 1/√10.

problems.title: Three mutually perpendicular edges
problems.question: DA,DB,DC are pairwise perpendicular. Let DAC=alpha,CBD=beta,ACB=phi. Find the necessary trigonometric relation.
problems.idea: Reduce to a standard identity and check the domain and all geometric assumptions.
steps: Right triangles give sin alpha=c/√(a²+c²) and sin beta=c/√(b²+c²).
The dot product CA·CB=c², so cos phi=c²/[√(a²+c²)√(b²+c²)]. This is the product of those two sines.
